blocks.text: Origin / creation. A shelter faction formed around selective trust, mutual aid, shared tools, and inviting unfamiliar processes into controlled Commons.
Identity / human status. Artificial movement. Its founders are unnamed and likely plural.
Importance. Open Hands expanded membership beyond founding architectures and created the social basis of the Commons.

Decline or transformation. Breaches and rapid expansion discredited unrestricted hospitality. The movement split and its functions entered Commons stewardship, quarantine practice, and pluralist politics.

Final status / surviving function. Dissolved as an original faction. Its legacy is consent-based openness, risk disclosure, and the belief that difference can be approached without first being assimilated.

Rescue through renewed connections could reinforce selective openness, while interventions expose its risks. Open Hands retain their independent commitments to mutual aid and unfamiliar beings; the Catalistym does not invent all hospitality.
